title: Football transfer rumours: Chelsea's Marcos Alonso back to Real Madrid?
trail: Paul Pogba to Barcelona? | Toby Alderweireld to Bayern Munich? | Gervinho to Parma? | Georges-Kévin N’Koudou to Mainz?
body: Having played just a solitary minute for Real Madrid’s first team back in April 2010, Marcos Alonso is being tenuously linked with a return to the club of his youth. After his only appearance – as a substitute, on for Gonzalo Higuaín in a 2-0 win over Racing Santander – for the senior team, Alonso went to on to play for Bolton, Fiorentina, Sunderland and then Chelsea, where his hair has recently developed a kind of lustrous, Michael Flatley-esque bouffant quality that appears to be attracting admiring “come hither” glances from the Bernabéu. With Chelsea precluded from buying players until January, they are unlikely to entertain any offers for the full-back and only time will tell how Alonso reacts to news of his former club’s apparent interest. Following his team’s European Super Cup defeat at the hands of their city rivals Atlético on Wednesday, Real’s director of institutional relations (no, us neither), Emilio Butragueño, added his two cents to the blizzard of speculation regarding the future of Luka Modric. Despite interest from Inter, Butragueño insisted the Croatian playmaker “could not be happier to continue playing for Real Madrid”, although the player’s agent, Marko Naletilić has begged to differ. “Modric didn’t just think about playing at Inter, he’s really thrilled by the idea of having as big role with the Nerazzurri,” said Natelic in an interview with Tuttosport. “I have a feeling that sooner or later, Modric will play in Italy. He grew up watching Serie A.” Paul Pogba’s relationship with José Mourinho continues to deteriorate, with claims of another new bust-up between the Manchester United midfielder and his boss being drip-fed to the media. Mourinho is reported to have told Pogba to hand in a transfer request if he wants to leave Old Trafford. By way of response, Pogba has supposedly announced he will only speak to the club through his agent, Mino Raiola. This latest squabble follows Pogba’s cryptic comments in the wake of United’s victory against Leicester on Friday, when he said “there are things I cannot say, otherwise I will get fined”. Merely alluding to “things” he couldn’t say seems to have been enough to send Mourinho into a full-on funk. The Portuguese subsequently demanded showdown talks which, by the sound of things, didn’t go tremendously well. Barcelona remain interested in Pogba, but are unlikely to make their move this summer. Exiled to the margins of Tottenham’s first team squad due to his lack of commitment, Toby Alderweireld is inching his way across Bayern Munich’s radar. With Jérôme Boateng on the verge of leaving the German champions for their French counterparts Paris Saint-Germain, the Mirror reports that Bayern have earmarked the 29-year-old Belgian as a potential replacement. Elsewhere in the Tottenham ranks, having spent the second half of last season on loan at Burnley where he failed to establish himself, Georges-Kévin N’Koudou once again finds himself surplus to Mauricio Pochettino’s requirements and is about to be farmed out to Mainz for the season. Former Arsenal and Roma striker Gervinho is on the verge of a return to Serie A with newly promoted Parma, who are hopeful of securing the Ivorian’s services from Chinese club Hebei Fortune. Meanwhile in Newcastle, Senegalese midfielder Henri Saivet is on the verge of signing for Turkish outfit Bursaspor on a season-long loan deal. Despite having three years left on his £35,000-per-week contract, the player is seen to have no future at Newcastle, who have been touting him around various clubs across the continent.
